messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: I cannot compile source code of version 2.0 in windows
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

You should be able to release RStan 2.0.1 at any point now.
That's one of the reasons we wanted to decouple Stan and RStan.

Whatever gets worked out on the Stan side for adaptation won't
affect the RStan interface.

Our hope is that any RStan with the same major and minor version (2.0
here) will work with any Stan version with matching major and minor
versions.

- Bob

>
> Hi Juan,
>
> I think the problem is with your configuration of R 3.0.2. The steps you followed to package RStan just
> repackages RStan and should be identical to downloading the rstan_2.0.0.tar.gz from
> https://github.com/stan-dev/__rstan/releases/download/v2.0.__0/rstan_2.0.0.tar.gz
> <https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.0.0/rstan_2.0.0.tar.gz>.
>
> When you install RStan from within R, your compiler does this:
>
> g++ -m64 -I"C:/R-30~1.2/include" -DNDEBUG -I"../inst/include/stansrc" -I"" -I"/unsupported" -I
> -I"../inst/include" -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS
> -I"C:/R-3.0.2/library/Rcpp/__include" -I"d:/RCompile/CRANpkg/__extralibs64/local/include" -O3 -c
> stanc.cpp -o stanc.o
>
>
> When it's installed properly, it should look like:
>
> g++ -m32 -I"C:/R/R-30~1.2/include" -I"../inst/include/stansrc"
> -I"../inst/include/stanlib/__eigen_3.2.0" -I"../inst/include/stanlib/__eigen_3.2.0/unsupported"
> -I../inst/include/stanlib/__boost_1.54.0 -I"../inst/include" -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE
> -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -I"C:/R/R-3.0.2/library/Rcpp/__include"
> -I"d:/RCompile/CRANpkg/__extralibs64/local/include" -O3 -Wall -mtune=core2 -c stanc.cpp -o stanc.o
>
>
>
> These are the differences, correct on the left, your configuration on the right:
>
> 1. -I"../inst/include/stanlib/__eigen_3.2.0" vs -I""
> 2. -I"../inst/include/stanlib/__eigen_3.2.0/unsupported" vs -I"/unsupported"
> 3. -I../inst/include/stanlib/__boost_1.54.0 vs -I
>
>
> So... I'm at a loss now. I'm not sure how the Boost and Eigen library locations in your makefiles have gotten lost.
>
> I think you mentioned that you reinstalled R. Is that true? Perhaps there's some interaction with environment
> variables stomping on the library locations? Can you check which environment variables have been set?
>
> Do you know of a way we can replicate your setup?
>
>
>
>
> Daniel
